text.insert: The accepted design gives each game one continuing harness worktree and durable state. Initial Sync establishes readiness; Run then alternates epochs with Sync. Epochs, save points, and timeline events preserve progress without opening or closing cycles. Runtime migration to this design is pending.

steps.text: Resolve the game configuration and prepare its canonical harness worktree.
Acquire and import configured knowledge sources, validate the build, and record the initial head and evidence.
Refresh target eligibility from the accepted source and report baseline.
Workers edit isolated game-specific Daytona workspaces and return code and evidence.
The host validates results and serializes accepted integration into the harness worktree.
Settle claims and integration, measure the accepted epoch result, and capture its save point.
Append the epoch boundary to the harness timeline and hand source authority to Sync.
Sync and Record the Next Boundary
Reconcile upstream and refresh knowledge according to each source policy.
Apply validated source changes and record prior and accepted heads. Record no-change completion without inventing a commit.
Capture required post-sync evidence, keeping upstream gains separate from epoch gains.
Refresh reports and board eligibility for the post-sync head.
Admit the next epoch only after Sync and required evidence succeed, unless paused.
Preserve durable state and timeline across pauses and process restarts. Conflicts or failed gates block admission.

text.insert: Worker summaries and attempts, merged PRs, Discord messages, and drift findings produce librarian tasks. The librarian proposes facts and relationships; the apply layer validates them before writing the shared knowledge base. Later workers receive a knowledge card and can query or render supporting records.
owns what workers receive and query.
owns dispatch coordination. Sync and run cannot mutate protected source concurrently. Their handoff settles the outgoing lease before the successor acquires authority.

PR publication is an operation on a verified source revision, not a third top-level lifecycle. PR splitting and campaign behavior remain a separate design task. This lifecycle decision does not itself publish a PR or implement new publishing behavior.
defines boundary evidence and the transfer of cycle responsibilities. Manual Sync while paused preserves the pause; successful Sync alone does not authorize worker resumption.
